display: Priya Naidoo, caseworker at a tenants' union in south Manchester. Ex-estate agent, now on the tenants' side. I handle damp, disrepair, deposits and section 21 notices, and I keep a casebook of 380 cases and a sheet of 412 landlords and agents.

signals.text: I'm three cases short of the 30 well-documented Levenshulme damp-and-mould cases I need, and the deadline to finalise the file is 14 October.
I'm looking for Levenshulme households with mould or damp who have photos, dated emails with the landlord or agent, or a medical letter, and who are willing to be in a collective file.
I have a meeting with the council's housing enforcement team on 28 October and want the file to show a pattern across landlords, not 23 separate complaints they can each shrug off.
I'm cleaning up a 412-row landlord and agent sheet. The same landlord often appears under four company names, and I need Companies House numbers to merge them.
I want to publish an anonymised 'worst agents' league table in the union newsletter. Legal says every entry needs two corroborated cases, so I need help checking that.

Tenants keep learning too late that once the council serves an improvement notice, a retaliatory no-fault eviction is blocked for six months. I want that sentence in front of people before the notice arrives.
Timing is the cruellest part of my job. People reach us after the eviction notice has already arrived, when the clock is tight.
Getting heating or repairs sorted often needs a formal request to environmental health. I'd like a simple way to get tenants to make that request early.
I'm double-booked on a weekend between a union 'know your rights' stall and my greyhound walking club, and I could use another volunteer for stalls.
I'm trying to learn Portuguese before a trip to Lisbon in April with my sister, and my study streak keeps slipping when casework piles up.
I'm on the allotment waiting list at number 61 with a six-year wait, so I'm growing cress on the windowsill and would like to find someone with shared growing space.
My rescue greyhound is scared of bin lorries and busy roads. I'd like to meet other owners of nervous rescue dogs.
Doing this work is heavy on me. I had a burnout break earlier this year and still see a counsellor monthly.
My own flat has a damp patch I haven't reported because I don't want to fight my landlord.

offers.text: A casebook of 380 closed and open cases since 2020, tagged by landlord, managing agent, ward and defect type. I can say whether a landlord or agent shows a repeat pattern.
I can explain how the Housing Act 2004 HHSRS process works, how Category 1 hazards get scored, and what the council's private-sector housing team will and won't act on.
I know the rule that once the council serves an improvement notice, the landlord can't serve a retaliatory section 21 for six months, and I can explain how to trigger it in practice.
Template letters for disrepair, deposit protection and Tenant Fees Act breaches.
Nine years inside estate agency in Didsbury. I know how listings, rent rises and agent excuses work from the inside.
Six years of contacts I can introduce you to once there's a concrete case: housing solicitors, environmental health officers and a local councillor on the housing committee.
A damp meter, a borrowed thermal camera and a phone camera. I know how to photograph mould, such as mould under fresh paint, so it works as evidence.
I can cover deposit-dispute drop-ins and run 'know your rights' stalls in south Manchester.
I can help organise a pattern-evidence file for a council enforcement meeting: how many cases, what documentation, and how to structure them.

catchers.hypo: My landlord painted over black mould in the back bedroom. I'm in Levenshulme and I have photos and dated emails. Is that any use to anyone?
catchers.can: Priya can add the household to the Levenshulme damp-and-mould file, advise on what evidence to gather, and show how it supports a collective case.
catchers.confirm: Is the property in Levenshulme or the surrounding area, with damp or mould, and does the tenant have dated photos or written complaints to the landlord or agent?

catchers.hypo: I got a no-fault eviction notice shortly after reporting mould to my landlord. I never asked anyone for help before. Is it too late?
catchers.can: Priya can check whether a council improvement notice is in place or can still be requested, explain the six-month protection, and say how tight the timing is. She'll refer on to a solicitor if the case needs court representation.
catchers.confirm: Did the tenant report the disrepair before the eviction notice arrived, and is the property in the Manchester area?

catchers.hypo: The same landlord seems to own several flats under different company names, and the agent ignores every repair request. How do I find out whether others are affected?
catchers.can: Priya can check her landlord and agent sheet for duplicates and a repeat pattern. Naming anyone publicly needs two corroborated cases first.
catchers.confirm: Do you have the landlord or agent's name or company number, and are the properties in Greater Manchester?

catchers.hypo: I'm a researcher or journalist looking at patterns of landlord neglect in Manchester. Is there any data I could use?
catchers.can: Priya can describe the shape of her casebook at t0, share anonymised patterns once a purpose is clear, and point to her published league table when it's ready.
catchers.confirm: Is the work about private-rented-sector disrepair in Greater Manchester, and will it anonymise tenants and avoid naming landlords without two corroborated cases?

catchers.hypo: I'm a housing solicitor who'd like to see a documented pattern of damp cases before talking to the council. Who has that?
catchers.can: Priya can share the Levenshulme case list structure once there's a concrete legal-support need. A solicitor friend of hers has already offered an hour at the enforcement meeting.
catchers.confirm: Is the solicitor willing to review case evidence without tenants' names or medical details, and does the work relate to private-rented-sector disrepair?

catchers.hypo: I'm on benefits and my landlord says I owe rent, but the flat has been damp for months. Who looks at both issues?
catchers.can: Priya's colleague Marcus, who shares her office and handles benefits cases, can look at the benefits side, and Priya can handle the disrepair side.
catchers.confirm: Does the tenant have both a benefits or rent-arrears issue and a disrepair problem, and live in south Manchester?

catchers.hypo: I teach primary school in Leeds and several of my pupils live in damp, mouldy homes. Is there anyone who can speak to parents about their rights?
catchers.can: Priya's sister Anita is a primary school teacher in Leeds, so she can be the point of contact for school-side questions. Priya can offer a general 'know your rights' talk or leaflet.
catchers.confirm: Is the request from a school or community group, and is it about tenants' rights in general and not individual case advice?

catchers.hypo: I'm a council officer or councillor trying to understand where private rented sector complaints cluster. Who's tracking this?
catchers.can: Priya can talk about the pattern at a high level and, once purpose and trust are clear, discuss the enforcement meeting and the case file.
catchers.confirm: Is the contact from a Greater Manchester council or housing committee, and is it about enforcement against repeat landlords or agents?

catchers.hypo: I run a community energy group and have damp or thermal imaging kit and volunteers. Would that help tenants with mould?
catchers.can: Priya already borrows a thermal camera from a community energy group and can coordinate surveys of damp homes, with tenants' consent.
catchers.confirm: Is the group in the Manchester area, and can it do surveys with tenant consent and share findings without naming tenants?

catchers.hypo: My rescue greyhound panics at bin lorries and I'm looking for people who've trained one through that. Any tips?
catchers.can: Priya's greyhound Mabel is a nervous three-year-old rescue in training with a trainer, and Priya can swap tips on treats, distance and gradual exposure. She also loves a radiator.
catchers.confirm: Is the dog a rescue greyhound or similar and afraid of loud noises or traffic, and are you in or near south Manchester?

forbids.text: I won't take cases that need court representation unless a solicitor is involved.
I can't see walk-ins outside the drop-in hours because of my caseload.
I work 9 to 5, four days a week.
I won't name a landlord or agent publicly without two corroborated cases.
I won't share tenants' names or addresses, or any client's medical details.

projects.text: A file of at least 30 well-documented damp and mould cases across three landlords and one managing agent, for the council's housing enforcement meeting on 28 October. The finalising deadline is 14 October.
roles_needed: Levenshulme tenants with mould or damp and documentation
community energy or damp survey helper

projects.name: Landlord and agent league table
projects.text: Cleaning and de-duplicating a 412-row sheet of landlords and agents, with Companies House numbers, into an anonymised newsletter league table. Every entry needs two corroborated cases.

policy.t1: When there's a concrete lead I'll share the improvement notice rule, case numbers, the Levenshulme file and the enforcement meeting.
policy.t2: Once trust is clear and the other party's identity is established, I'll share how I cope with the work and my own flat.
policy.never: Tenants' names and addresses, and any medical details of clients.
